To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of intramembranour particles on P faces is much higher than on E faces, and that the number of these particles in the luminal part of the plasma membrane is lower than in the lateral part of the plasma membranes.
the density of IMPs in the plasma membrane of liver cells is higher on P faces than on E faces, and that the density of the IMPs is higher in lateral than in luminal regions of the plasma membrane.
The P and E faces of the plasma membrane of normal hepatocytes are characterized by the presence, respectively, of a large number of IMPs and by the presence of tight junctions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the ultrastructural alterations of the plasma membranes of hepatocyte after bile duct liga-tion.
the study of the morphology of plasma cell membranes of hepatocytes in normal and in cholestatic liver.
the ultrastructural changes in the plasma membrane of hepatocytes after extrahepatic cholestasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tight junction is a complex structure composed of a network of interdigitating strands.
the plasma membrane of the hepatocytes of normal adult rat liver is characterized by a low density of IMPs and by the presence of tight junctions, which are continuous and of a regular structure.

in normal liver cells the P face is characterized by a greater number of intramembranouss particles, by the presence of a higher density of IMPs in the lateral region, by the presence in the same region of a greater number of IMPs in microvilli, and by a higher number of tight junctions with a more regular structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
after bile duct liga- tion, there is a marked increase in the density of IMPs in the E faces of plasma membranes.

in cholestatic liver cells the P face is characterized by a significant decrease in the number and density of intramembranously located particles, whereas in the E face the number and density remain unchanged or increase slightly.
in normal liver cells the P faces of the plasma membrane show more intramembranously located particles than the E faces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tight junctions are the only sites in which the plasma membrane is continuous around the cell, thus providing a barrier to the passage of substances across cell membranes.
the density and distribution of IMPs in hepatocyte plasma membranes are altered by cholestasis.
bile duct ligation results in a marked increase in the density of IMPs in the P face and in an increase in the number of tight junctions.
